audit.why: Full phases[].side, content win[] and packet.levelChart all read Akali on all seven rows, and that matches the kit: Xerath has no dash, no blink and one point of CC, so Akali is favoured at every stage. Ratings 7-8/10 are consistent with the 52.1% win rate and the FAVOURED tag. No chart edit proposed.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spike text described a level 6 window around Xerath 'channelling' and a first-item window around out-racing 'his short-range blink'.
audit.why: Rite of the Arcane immobilizes Xerath himself for its duration — that is the real level 6 spike and it is far stronger than what was written. The first-item spike needed no blink premise because Xerath has none.
audit.corrected: Level 6 spike now states that the ult pins him in place; the first-item spike now names Shocking Orb as the only thing between Akali and him.

audit.whatIsWrong: FABRICATED KIT. The text repeatedly gave Xerath a blink ('his short blink', 'his short-range Arcanopulse blink cooldown', 'faster than he can reposition with his short-range blink'), and called his CC a ROOT from an ability named 'Mage Chains'. It also named his W barrage 'Arcane Barrage'.
audit.why: Xerath's real kit is Mana Surge (P), Arcanopulse (Q, 750, 9/8/7/6/5s), Eye of Destruction (W, 1000, 14/13/12/11/10s), Shocking Orb (E, 1050, 13/12.5/12/11.5/11s, a STUN not a root) and Rite of the Arcane (R, 130/115/100s). There is no blink and no ability called Mage Chains or Arcane Barrage anywhere in the kit. Telling an Akali player to 'punish his blink cooldown' is advice about a button that does not exist, and 'root' vs 'stun' changes whether Flash answers it.
audit.corrected: Every blink reference removed and replaced with the true statement that Xerath has zero mobility; Mage Chains replaced with Shocking Orb throughout and correctly described as a stun; Arcane Barrage replaced with Eye of Destruction.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns and dosFull[2].d gave no real numbers and dosFull[2].d called it a 'fifteen-second invitation'.
audit.why: Shocking Orb is 13s at rank 1 and only drops to 11s at rank 5 — unusually flat, which is why the window recurs so reliably. Fifteen seconds was wrong in the player's favour.
audit.corrected: Real per-rank numbers written into breakdown.cooldowns; the invitation corrected to thirteen seconds.

audit.whatIsWrong: enemyWin and breakdown.carry were structural templates.
audit.why: 'wins by landing X, denying your pattern, and keeping the fight at a distance your kit resents' and 'Carry through deletions — one carry per fight' paste onto any enemy.
audit.corrected: Both regrounded on Xerath's actual ranges and his total lack of mobility.

edits.before: Xerath wins by landing Shocking Orb (Stun), denying your pattern, and keeping the fight at a distance your kit resents.
edits.after: Xerath wins by landing Shocking Orb at 1050, chaining Eye of Destruction into Arcanopulse, and killing you before you close.

edits.before: - Xerath Shocking Orb (Stun): matchup-defining — His only CC — dodge the orb and his artillery never converts into a kill. Step up only on its downtime. - Budget W Twilight Shroud for emergencies and the R for opportunities — never swap them.
edits.after: - Shocking Orb: 13s at rank 1 and only 11s maxed — his one point of CC, and this lane is that window. - Eye of Destruction slows from 1000 on a 14s clock. - Rite of the Arcane immobilizes Xerath himself while it fires: that is your entry.

edits.before: Carry through deletions — one carry per fight, every fight; the shroud buys the time and the resets pay the exit.
edits.after: Xerath is the softest deletion in mid — no dash, no blink, no self-peel once Shocking Orb is spent. Go straight through.

edits.before: Xerath burns Shocking Orb (Stun) on nothing — take the fifteen-second invitation.
edits.after: Xerath burns Shocking Orb on a minion — take the thirteen-second invitation.

edits.before: Your dash-in combo at level 3 closes the gap before his short blink can reposition him to safety.
edits.after: Your dash-in combo at level 3 closes the gap for good — Xerath has no dash or blink to remake it.

edits.before: Your first-item reset lets you dash in twice, keeping pace with his repositioning attempts.
edits.after: Your first-item reset lets you dash in twice, and only Flash answers either entry.

edits.before: Once you have your dash-and-flip combo you can close the gap on his root-and-poke pattern before Arcane Barrage lands a second time, since he has zero mobility to reposition.
edits.after: Once you have the dash-and-flip combo you close on his poke pattern before Eye of Destruction lands a second time — he has zero mobility, so a missed Shocking Orb is a free all-in.

edits.before: Your Perfect Execution reset still kills him through his ultimate's damage window, since he needs to channel Rite of the Arcane and can't peel while doing it.
edits.after: Perfect Execution kills him straight through Rite of the Arcane, because the ult immobilizes Xerath himself — once he starts firing he cannot walk away from you.

edits.before: A burst item cooldown reset lets you dash in twice in one trade, closing distance faster than he can reposition with his short-range blink.
edits.after: A burst item spike lets you dash in twice in one trade, and with no dash of his own the only thing standing between you is Shocking Orb.

edits.before: Xerath has huge range advantage but no mobility at levels 1-2, so you win the lane by weaving through minion waves and using Shroud to approach without giving him a clean root target.
edits.after: Xerath has huge range but no mobility at levels 1-2, so weave through the wave and use Shroud to approach without giving Shocking Orb a clean target — his stun is the only thing that stops you.

edits.before: From level 3 your dash-and-burst combo closes distance faster than his short blink can reposition, and since Mage Chains has a real cooldown, punishing him right after a missed root wins the all-in outright.
edits.after: From level 3 your dash-and-burst combo closes distance he has no dash or blink to remake, and Shocking Orb is 13 seconds at rank 1, so punishing him right after a missed stun wins the all-in outright.

edits.before: Punish his short-range Arcanopulse blink cooldown the moment he uses it to reposition
edits.after: Punish the 13-second Shocking Orb window the moment he whiffs the stun on you

edits.before: All-in immediately once he's out of mana or has used Mage Chains for poke, not control
edits.after: All-in immediately once he's out of mana or has spent Shocking Orb on the wave

edits.before: Root you with Mage Chains from max range to set up a full poke combo
edits.after: Stun you with Shocking Orb at 1050 range to set up a full poke combo

edits.before: Kite using his short blink to keep you outside melee range as long as possible
edits.after: Hold Shocking Orb as his one answer and keep you outside 550 as long as he can

notes: This matchup carried the worst fabrication found in my slice: Xerath was given a blink he does not have, in four separate places, and his stun was called a ROOT belonging to an ability named 'Mage Chains' — not a Xerath ability. His W was also called 'Arcane Barrage'. All corrected against the kit (Mana Surge / Arcanopulse / Eye of Destruction / Shocking Orb / Rite of the Arcane). The packet suspectName 'Your Perfect Execution' is a FALSE POSITIVE — Perfect Execution is Akali's real R. Level chart needed no work: all three sources already agree on Akali x7. Derived-flag caution: Xerath's R carries the 'channel: interruptible — any CC cancels it' flag, but Riot's own text only says he immobilizes himself. I wrote the immobilisation, which the text supports, and did NOT write that CC cancels it. Unverified and therefore left alone: whether Shocking Orb's stun can be Flashed after the cast, whether Twilight Shroud's untargetability drops an in-flight Shocking Orb, and whether Akali's R recast can be buffered during the stun.
